stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct model on Hugging Face.
It pertains to the text-generation pipeline, indicating its use in large language model applications.
The associated tags confirm its relevance to major AI components like transformers and Llama.

stories.title: SpaceX is coming for T-Mobile, AT&T and Verizon
stories.author: Thomas Ricker
bullet_points: SpaceX is planning to develop a terrestrial mobile network.
The goal of this new network is to directly compete with major US carriers (T-Mobile, AT&T, Verizon).
The announcement was made by SpaceX leadership during their recent earnings call.

stories.title: AMD’s data center business is booming while gaming takes a backseat
stories.author: Stevie Bonifield
bullet_points: AMD's data center revenue experienced massive growth, more than doubling year-over-year.
The surge is directly attributed to high demand for AI computing capacity.
This growth highlights a significant industry shift favoring AI infrastructure over traditional gaming segments for AMD.

stories.title: SpaceX made more revenue as an AI company than a space company
stories.author: Elizabeth Lopatto
bullet_points: SpaceX's AI revenue has seen a significant surge, growing over threefold to $2.6 billion.
This revenue growth is primarily driven by providing compute resources to other AI companies.
The AI division is highlighted in SpaceX's filings as a major source of its business.

stories.title: Texas halts data center connections to power grid amid overwhelming demand
stories.author: Jeremy Hsu
bullet_points: Texas is pausing data center connections to the power grid due to overwhelming demand.
This development directly contradicts the state's recent promotion of Texas as an AI 'epicenter'.
The story highlights the critical infrastructure challenges associated with the rapid expansion of AI and data center usage.

stories.title: US company’s AI lets Ukraine’s cheap kamikaze drones track targets on their own
stories.author: Jeremy Hsu
bullet_points: A US company is providing advanced AI capabilities to Ukraine's inexpensive kamikaze drones.
The deal involves equipping 50,000 Ukrainian drones with US-developed autonomous targeting AI.
The agreement is valued at $100 million, highlighting the integration of cutting-edge AI into tactical military hardware.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Highlights the trending status of the DeepSeek-R1 model on Hugging Face Benchmarks.
The model is categorized under text-generation and conversational AI pipelines.
It utilizes standard ML components like transformers and safetensors.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Meta-Llama-3-8B model on Hugging Face Benchmarks.
The model is categorized under text-generation pipelines, indicating its primary function.
Key associated technologies include transformers, safetensors, and the Llama architecture.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a platform for running open models, has secured significant funding.
The company raised $88 million from prominent investors including Y Combinator and Benchmark.
Ollama currently serves a large developer base of 8.9 million users.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 performance is significantly boosted in Ollama 0.31 when running on Apple Silicon.
The speed improvement is achieved through the implementation of Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) powered by MLX.
Coding agent performance saw up to a 90% speed increase, as validated by the Aider polyglot benchmark.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is attributed to updates in the MLX engine.
Improvements include faster response times, higher output quality, and reduced memory usage.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA is introducing Nemotron 3 Ultra, a new model architecture.
The model is specifically engineered for high-throughput reasoning tasks.
It is designed to support complex, long-running agent workflows.

stories.title: OpenJarvis: a local-first personal AI is now available to run with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenJarvis v1.0 is released, providing an open-source framework for personal AI agents.
The framework emphasizes a 'local-first' approach, allowing AI to run entirely on user hardware.
It features built-in support for Ollama, facilitating the use of local LLMs.

stories.title: Ollama is now powered by MLX on Apple Silicon in preview
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a popular local LLM runner, is integrating MLX for performance optimization.
This integration specifically targets Apple Silicon hardware, leveraging Apple's native ML framework.
The feature is currently available in a preview state, indicating early adoption and performance testing.

stories.title: OpenClaw
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenClaw is a personal AI assistant designed to integrate with messaging applications.
It utilizes local AI coding agents, emphasizing on-device processing for privacy and speed.
The core value proposition is connecting messaging workflows directly to local, private AI capabilities.

stories.title: Video-DeepResearch: Towards the Next-Generation Multimodal Deepresearch Agent
stories.author: Feng Zhao
bullet_points: Introduces Video-DeepResearch (Video-DR), a new multimodal agent designed to process continuous video streams.
Addresses critical limitations in current agents, specifically modality bias (over-reliance on text search) and parametric knowledge leakage.
Focuses on achieving dense spatiotemporal grounding combined with open-web exploration capabilities.

stories.title: ParVL: Parallel Scaling and Expandable Compute Allocation for Multimodal LLMs
stories.author: Wenwei Zhang
bullet_points: Introduces ParVL, a new scaling framework designed for Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs).
Addresses limitations in current MLLM scaling by moving beyond simple parameter or sequential inference expansion.
Key innovation is allowing flexible, task-specific allocation of compute resources between the Vision Transformer and LLM components.

stories.title: WorldCup Arena: Prospective, Leakage-Free Evaluation of Frontier LLMs on a Live Tournament
stories.author: Zhangyang Qi
bullet_points: Introduces a novel, prospective evaluation methodology for frontier LLMs, moving beyond traditional retrospective benchmarking.
Tests six advanced LLMs (with web search capabilities) by having them make real-time, pre-match predictions for the 2026 FIFA World Cup.
Addresses the critical issue of LLM memorization in forecasting by evaluating performance on live, unfolding events.

stories.title: Mistral's Shieldstral: 3B open-weights model for multimodal moderation
stories.author: riadsila
bullet_points: Mistral has released Shieldstral, a new 3B open-weights model.
The model is specifically designed for multimodal moderation tasks.
This contributes to the growing trend of open-source models being applied to safety and content filtering.

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 release brings performance improvements and expanded GGUF model compatibility.
The update leverages llama.cpp to broaden model support across various hardware configurations.
It enhances Ollama's MLX engine specifically for better performance on Apple silicon.

stories.title: Subagents and web search in Claude Code
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has integrated support for subagents within Claude Code.
The update also introduces web search capabilities to Claude Code via Ollama.
This enhances the functionality of local LLM deployments by adding advanced reasoning and information retrieval.

stories.title: Now you can securely link multiple phones to one Signal account
stories.author: Stevie Bonifield
bullet_points: Signal now allows users to link multiple mobile phones (Android/iPhone) to a single account.
This feature expands device linking beyond existing support for PCs and iPads.
Users can now check and respond to messages across all linked devices for enhanced accessibility.

stories.title: EA is now a private company
stories.author: Jay Peters
bullet_points: Electronic Arts (EA) has officially transitioned from a public to a private company.
The privatization was completed via a $55 billion deal.
The investment group includes Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund (PIF) and Silver Lake.

stories.title: China is Tesla's cash cow, but for how much longer?
stories.author: Jonathan M. Gitlin
bullet_points: Tesla's Shanghai factory is currently operating at peak capacity.
The article suggests that China may be a crucial revenue driver for Tesla.
There are indications that Tesla might eventually reduce its reliance on the Chinese market.

stories.title: OpenAI says Apple's trade secrets lawsuit is "aggressive and oddly personal"
stories.author: Jamie John, Financial Times
bullet_points: OpenAI publicly criticized Apple's lawsuit, labeling it "aggressive and oddly personal."
OpenAI explicitly denied possessing or needing any of Apple's alleged trade secrets.
The incident highlights ongoing legal tensions between major AI and established tech giants.

stories.title: TurnSight: Turn-Level Hindsight Self-Distillation for Tool-Integrated Reasoning
stories.author: Jun Xu
bullet_points: Introduces 'TurnSight,' a novel method for self-distillation in Tool-Integrated Reasoning (TIR) for LLMs.
Addresses the limitation of trajectory-level supervision in TIR, which hinders fine-grained credit assignment in complex, long-horizon tasks.
Proposes using teacher branches with privileged context to generate denser training signals, moving beyond reliance on ground-truth answers or retrieved skills.

stories.title: Test-Time Scaling in Reasoning LLMs: Inference Regimes, Evaluation, and Reproducibility
stories.author: Vipin Chaudhary
bullet_points: The paper investigates 'test-time scaling' in Reasoning LLMs, showing that increased inference-time compute improves problem-solving ability.
Test-time scaling encompasses various inference algorithms, including trajectory extension, candidate sampling/aggregation, and state-space search.
The research highlights that these different inference procedures have distinct statistical structures, compute costs, and failure modes.

stories.title: Can Large Language Models Recover Semantic Optimization Opportunities That Compilers Miss?
stories.author: Chunwei Xia
bullet_points: The research investigates if Large Language Models (LLMs) can recover semantic optimization opportunities that traditional compilers overlook.
The core problem addressed is the inability of compilers to perform transformations when necessary semantics are missing from the program representation.
A new executable benchmark, SeGaBench, is introduced to test LLMs across various low-level and high-level semantic lifting scenarios in C/C++.

stories.title: ReflectRL: Learning from Golden Negative Trajectories via Reflective-to-Direct Reasoning
stories.author: Tat-Seng Chua
bullet_points: Introduces ReflectRL, a method to leverage 'Golden Negative Trajectories' from expert models.
Addresses a limitation in current trajectory-guided LLM training where expert failures are typically discarded.
Proposes that failed expert trajectories can still provide valuable supervision for improving LLM reasoning.

stories.title: Should We Type or Talk to LLM Agents? A Comprehensive Study of Voice and Keyboard Input Perturbations
stories.author: Jesse Thomason
bullet_points: The study investigates how different human input methods (typing vs. speaking) affect Large Language Model (LLM) performance.
It introduces HIVE, a suite of perturbations designed to simulate real-world input noise, including orthographic noise and voice disfluencies.
The research aims to evaluate the robustness of LLMs when faced with variations inherent in voice transcription and keyboard entry.

stories.title: Separating quantum circuits from classical LLMs
stories.author: Rik Sengupta
bullet_points: The research proves unconditional separations between low-depth quantum computation ($	extsf{QNC}^0$) and classical LLM architectures.
The separation is demonstrated in both prediction and generation regimes of modern language models.
A specific distributional separation is provided, showing a distribution sampleable by constant-depth quantum circuits that classical models cannot easily replicate.

stories.title: Interpretable Adaptive Sampling for LLM Test-Time Scaling
stories.author: Ali Jannesari
bullet_points: Addresses the inefficiency of fixed compute budgets in LLM test-time scaling.
Proposes an 'adaptive test-time scaling' method using a lightweight fuzzy controller.
The controller uses interpretable signals, like estimated prompt complexity, to dynamically allocate samples.

stories.title: A game theory for foundation models shows new paths to rational cooperation through similarity inference
stories.author: Blaise Agüera y Arcas
bullet_points: The paper proposes a new game theory framework specifically designed for foundation models.
It addresses the limitation of classical game theory, which assumes 'decoupled agency,' contrasting with modern, jointly predictive AI agents.
The research aims to establish principles for rational cooperation among autonomous agents integrated into complex systems.

stories.title: TACT: Taxonomy-Aligned Post-Training for Pedagogically Adaptive English Tutoring
stories.author: Zixin Chen
bullet_points: The paper introduces TACT, a method for making LLMs act as pedagogically adaptive English tutors.
Current LLM-based ESL tutoring lacks the ability to select appropriate teaching actions based on learner behavior.
TACT aims to integrate principles from human-tutoring research into LLM training for better ESL support.

stories.title: Test-Time Scaling in Reasoning LLMs: Inference Regimes, Evaluation, and Reproducibility
stories.author: Vipin Chaudhary
bullet_points: The paper addresses 'test-time scaling' in Large Language Models (LLMs), showing that increased inference compute can improve reasoning capabilities.
Test-time scaling encompasses diverse inference algorithms, including trajectory extension, candidate sampling/aggregation, and state search.
The research highlights that these different inference procedures have distinct statistical structures, compute accounting methods, and failure modes.

stories.title: Logic Before Language: Pre-pretraining on Formal Derivations Fosters Skill Acquisition and Compressibility
stories.author: Marco Valentino
bullet_points: The research proposes pre-pretraining Language Models (LMs) using formal derivations (symbolic data) to enhance natural language acquisition.
Existing pre-pretraining methods are criticized for relying on narrow primitives that lack the expressive power of natural language.
The study aims to overcome limitations in prior work, specifically regarding small token budgets and limited insight into skill emergence.

stories.title: Latent Reward Registers for Diffusion Preference Alignment
stories.author: Peiqin Sun
bullet_points: Addresses the temporal credit-assignment problem in aligning diffusion models with human preferences.
Introduces 'Latent Reward Registers' to estimate terminal preference directly from intermediate noisy latents.
Implements this via prepending learnable, position-free register tokens to a frozen Diffusion Transformer (DiT).

stories.title: PRISM: Powerful Time Series to Image (TS2I) Representations for Multivariate Anomaly Detection
stories.author: Roberto Corizzo
bullet_points: Addresses the challenge of representation choice in multivariate Time Series Anomaly Detection (TSAD).
Proposes PRISM, a method to transform time series data into image representations for TSAD.
Investigates whether vision backbones can achieve performance comparable to traditional time-domain methods in this domain.

stories.title: SocietyBench: Forecasting Counterfactual Social-World Evolution
stories.author: Zhangyang Qi
bullet_points: Introduces SocietyBench, a new benchmark designed to test LLMs' ability to forecast real-world social and world events.
Addresses a gap in current LLM evaluation, which heavily focuses on task completion (e.g., coding, GUI operation) rather than social understanding.
The benchmark aggregates and analyzes data from five different social media and web news platforms based on a single event topic.

stories.title: TurnSight: Turn-Level Hindsight Self-Distillation for Tool-Integrated Reasoning
stories.author: Jun Xu
bullet_points: Introduces 'TurnSight,' a method for self-distillation specifically designed for Tool-Integrated Reasoning (TIR) in LLMs.
Addresses the limitation of trajectory-level supervision in TIR, which hinders fine-grained credit assignment in long tasks.
Proposes using teacher branches with privileged context to provide denser training signals, moving beyond reliance on ground-truth answers.

stories.title: PAST-Bench: Benchmarking the Foundations of Recursive Self-Improvement in Personal Agents
stories.author: Ling Yang
bullet_points: Introduces PAST-Bench, a new benchmark specifically designed to test recursive self-improvement in AI agents.
Focuses on the capability of personal AI agents to improve future behavior based on accumulated past experience (preferences, history, skills).
Addresses a gap in current research by systematically testing whether retained experience leads to genuine performance improvement over time.

stories.title: Agogic: Performance-Timed Music Tokens for LLM-Native Text-to-Symbolic-Music Generation
stories.author: Ruqi Huang
bullet_points: The research introduces 'Agogic,' a method for performance-timed music tokens designed for LLM-native text-to-symbolic-music generation.
The study isolates the impact of different music tokenizations by fixing other model parameters (like Qwen3.5, data, and decoding).
The findings suggest that the choice of representation (tokenization) is a more critical factor than model size in determining generation quality.

stories.title: When Attention Goes Blind: Numerical Failure in ALiBi Positional Encodings
stories.author: Gerhard Heyer
bullet_points: Identifies a critical, previously overlooked failure mode in ALiBi positional encodings.
The failure involves linear bias scaling underflowing floating-point precision, effectively zeroing out attention weights.
The research analyzes the impact and proposes four mitigation strategies for state-of-the-art models using ALiBi.

stories.title: HalluTruthQA-4K: A Fine-Grained Corpus and Annotation Process for Arabic Hallucination Detection and Truth Verification
stories.author: Abdenour Hadid
bullet_points: Introduces HalluTruthQA-4K, a new, expanded corpus specifically designed for Arabic language processing.
Addresses the limitation of existing resources by moving beyond binary (hallucinated/not hallucinated) labeling.
Focuses on fine-grained detection, providing details on erroneous content, error reasons, and correct facts in LLM outputs.

stories.title: Logic Before Language: Pre-pretraining on Formal Derivations Fosters Skill Acquisition and Compressibility
stories.author: Marco Valentino
bullet_points: The research proposes pre-pretraining Language Models (LMs) using formal derivations (symbolic data) to enhance natural language acquisition.
Existing pre-pretraining methods are limited by narrow primitives and small token budgets, failing to capture natural language's full expressive capacity.
The study aims to address these limitations by introducing a new logic pre-pretraining approach to better understand skill emergence in LMs.

stories.title: Zero-Mem: Zero-Token Memory Operations for LLM Agents
stories.author: theanonymousone
bullet_points: Introduces 'Zero-Mem,' a novel approach for memory operations in LLM agents.
Focuses on achieving 'Zero-Token' memory usage, suggesting efficiency gains.
Addresses a core challenge in scaling and deploying sophisticated LLM agents.

stories.title: IP and DNS Leaks in WebKit Affecting Proxy Browsers and iCloud Private Relay
stories.author: lapcat
bullet_points: WebKit vulnerabilities were found concerning IP and DNS leaks.
The leaks specifically affect proxy browsers and Apple's iCloud Private Relay.
This represents a security flaw impacting privacy-focused browsing technologies.

stories.title: rust-lang/rust is adopting an LLM policy
stories.author: blog.rust-lang.org via wezm
bullet_points: The Rust programming language community is formalizing a policy regarding the use of Large Language Models (LLMs).
This indicates a growing need for guidelines as AI tools become integrated into software development workflows.
The adoption of such a policy reflects the broader industry shift toward leveraging AI in coding and development practices.

stories.title: I type-check AI-generated SDK code against the real package. Claude refused a third of my Stripe tasks.
stories.author: kalpitrathore
bullet_points: A developer built 'SDKProof' to validate AI-generated SDK code against actual package implementations.
The tool highlights issues where AI models (specifically Claude) failed to correctly generate functional code for complex tasks (e.g., Stripe integration).
The story addresses the growing need for rigorous validation and testing of code produced by AI coding agents.

stories.title: Stop Trusting Vibes: A Reproducible Harness for Comparing AI Coding Models on Your Own Codebase
stories.author: devx_6522
bullet_points: Addresses the common flaw in AI coding model comparisons: lack of relevance to individual developer needs.
Proposes a 'reproducible harness' to allow users to benchmark AI models against their specific codebases.
Focuses on practical, empirical evaluation rather than anecdotal or generalized performance claims.

stories.title: Stop Vibes-Testing AI Coding Models: A Repeatable Evaluation Suite You Can Run for Free
stories.author: datars_7274
bullet_points: Addresses the common, subjective method developers use to test AI coding models (e.g., simple prompt testing).
Proposes a standardized, repeatable evaluation suite for objectively benchmarking AI coding performance.
The tool is available for free, making rigorous testing accessible to the developer community.

stories.title: Stop Guessing: A Reproducible Harness for Evaluating Free AI Coding Models on Your Own Repo
stories.author: byteio_501
bullet_points: Addresses the subjective nature of comparing AI coding models.
Proposes a reproducible harness for objective evaluation.
Focuses on testing models directly against a user's own codebase.
